**Part A - how I'd handle the three cases** (one sentence each, as asked):

**Confluences:** a junction breaks every branch that meets it, so a reach is a maximal run of channel between two topological events (junction, dangle, or component end) - though here that rule is nearly inert, since all 5 junctions are internal to fid 4, 6 and 8 and no feature touches another, so confluence-driven and one-part-one-reach converge on the same 13 reaches.

**Short stubs:** a leftover reach shorter than one full spacing gets merged into its longest adjacent reach at the shared junction rather than surviving to carry 2 transects and a mostly-empty plate; an isolated stub with no adjacent reach (8.2, 6.1, 6.3, 8.0) has nothing to merge into, so it survives and is flagged `short_reach`.
